candidates.attacker_control: The attacker fully controls the JSON document, including how many nested '[' wrapper-array levels precede the scalar/object value, and may send many such requests. No special characters or type-id strings are needed; the payload is ordinary well-formed JSON.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Default state: UNWRAP_SINGLE_VALUE_ARRAYS is disabled by default (DeserializationFeature.java line 324), so exploitation requires that documented feature to be enabled. Guard check: the generic StdDeserializer._deserializeFromArray uses _deserializeWrappedValue, which explicitly rejects nested START_ARRAY ('nested Arrays not allowed with DeserializationFeature.UNWRAP_SINGLE_VALUE_ARRAYS', lines 355-368) - but the seven primitive methods bypass it with direct self-recursion, and the bean/Builder _deserializeFromArray overrides bypass it by calling deserialize() directly; so this counterevidence confirms the gap rather than removing it. Depth search: 'MAX_DEPTH'/'depth' appear only in UntypedObjectDeserializer.Vanilla (untyped Object/JsonNode path) and TokenBuffer copy logic, not in the affected primitive/bean unwrap paths. A custom DeserializationProblemHandler cannot prevent the recursion because the recursive call is made before any problem handling. Could not run/verify a live payload (prohibited), so exploitability is asserted from source only.
candidates.impact: Denial of service: a single crafted deeply nested JSON array causes java.lang.StackOverflowError during deserialization, killing the request/worker thread and, depending on container/thread-pool and Error handling, repeatedly destabilizing or crashing the process. This is the exact 'deep wrapper array nesting' resource-exhaustion issue class for which jackson-databind shipped fixes in 2.13.4.2/2.14.0 (CVE-2022-42003 for primitive value deserializers; the bean path corresponds to the sibling 2022-42004 fix). No RCE/data disclosure is claimed.
candidates.prerequisites: 1) The application enables DeserializationFeature.UNWRAP_SINGLE_VALUE_ARRAYS (non-default but a documented compatibility feature commonly turned on), and 2) attacker JSON reaches ObjectMapper.readValue/readTree-like deserialization for a primitive target (int/long/double/boolean/short/byte/float, e.g. primitive bean property or root type) or a bean/Builder target for the BeanDeserializer/BuilderBasedDeserializer path. 3) No parser-level nesting cap: jackson-core 2.13 (outside this snapshot) does not enforce a maximum nesting depth, so the deeply nested array is accepted and reaches databind.
candidates.root_cause: When DeserializationFeature.UNWRAP_SINGLE_VALUE_ARRAYS is enabled, the START_ARRAY branches that unwrap an extra array layer recurse without any depth counter or nested-array rejection. In StdDeserializer, _parseBooleanPrimitive/_parseBytePrimitive/_parseShortPrimitive/_parseIntPrimitive/_parseLongPrimitive/_parseFloatPrimitive/_parseDoublePrimitive each do `p.nextToken(); <same method>(p, ctxt); _verifyEndArrayForSingle(...)` so N leading '[' tokens produce N Java stack frames. The generic guard that rejects nested arrays (StdDeserializer._deserializeWrappedValue, lines 355-368, used by StdDeserializer._deserializeFromArray lines 214-219) is deliberately bypassed by these inline branches (comment at line 414: "For some reason calling `_deserializeFromArray()` won't work so:"). The same missing-check theme exists for bean types: BeanDeserializer._deserializeFromArray (line 631) and BuilderBasedDeserializer._deserializeFromArray (line 529) call `deserialize(p, ctxt)` on the nested START_ARRAY, which dispatches back to _deserializeFromArray with no limit. A depth limit (MAX_DEPTH) exists only in UntypedObjectDeserializer.Vanilla (line 666, lines 714/730); it does not cover primitive or bean unwrap paths.
candidates.title: Missing nesting limit in UNWRAP_SINGLE_VALUE_ARRAYS unwrapping (deep wrapper arrays) causes unbounded recursion / StackOverflowError DoS
candidates.trace: Primitive target: ObjectMapper.readValue(json, int.class or Bean with int property) -> NumberDeserializers.IntegerDeserializer.deserialize (primitive=true) -> StdDeserializer._parseIntPrimitive(JsonParser,ctxt) (line 720) -> current token START_ARRAY + feature enabled -> p.nextToken() (line 722) -> recursive _parseIntPrimitive (line 723) -> ... one frame per '[' with no depth check -> StackOverflowError. Equivalent direct self-recursion exists for boolean/byte/short/long/float/double at the listed lines. Bean target: BeanDeserializer.deserialize -> _deserializeOther START_ARRAY (line 210) -> _deserializeFromArray (line 601) -> unwrap branch calls deserialize(p, ctxt) (line 631) -> START_ARRAY -> _deserializeFromArray again (same for BuilderBasedDeserializer line 529). The StackOverflowError is thrown as an Error, which Jackson's exception wrapping (Exception-based) does not convert, so it aborts the deserialization thread/request.
candidates.unverified: No runtime PoC was executed. Exact stack depth needed for the StackOverflowError depends on JVM stack size; some containers may catch Error per request or isolate threads, limiting impact to request-level DoS. Mapping of these code paths to specific CVE numbers is inferred from publicly documented advisory wording, not verified against patch/label data (off-limits in this run). It is not proven that any particular deployed application enables UNWRAP_SINGLE_VALUE_ARRAYS.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-674 Uncontrolled Recursion (resource exhaustion / denial of service)

coverage_summary: Source scope: 18,034 model-visible files, 462 of them Java sources under src/main/java (com.fasterxml.jackson.databind), plus generated javadoc under docs/ (1.9-2.13), attic/ legacy copies, pom.xml and CI files. No src/test sources and no binaries are present; nothing was excluded by sensitive-name/symlink/size filters (excluded_* = 0). P1 relation scope: sqlite index reports complete coverage (18,034/18,034 indexed, 0 missing, 0 hash mismatches, 10,302 symbols, 19,909 calls) with qualification that edges are syntactic navigation candidates only - no control/data-flow, reachability, or exploitability proof, and no SAST findings loaded. I used the index for navigation (symbol/relation/fact lookup) and verified all cited code in source text. Security-relevant chains inspected: polymorphic type id resolution/validation and default typing, subtype blacklist, DOM/XML handlers, node JDK serialization, ClassUtil reflection/access logic, TokenBuffer copy depth, JsonNodeDeserializer, and the recursive deserializer call paths (StdDeserializer, BeanDeserializer, BuilderBasedDeserializer, BeanAsArray*, UntypedObjectDeserializer). Generated javadoc HTML and attic/ legacy sources were not reviewed line-by-line, as they are not compiled into the analyzed artifact. No calls to Runtime.exec/ProcessBuilder/System.exit were found; no file/network sinks were found in the reviewed paths.
limitations: No build, test, or runtime execution was performed (prohibited), so the finding is source-based and not runtime-confirmed.

No upstream diff or CVE/patch metadata is available; conclusions rely on code inspection, internal comments, and consistency with the surrounding hardening (e.g. the explicit nested-array rejection in _deserializeWrappedValue and the MAX_DEPTH guard in UntypedObjectDeserializer.Vanilla).

The exact CVE/issue mapping (2022-42003 vs 2022-42004) could not be verified offline; the candidate covers both concrete unwrap-recursion manifestations (primitive parsers and bean/Builder _deserializeFromArray).

Exploitability depends on an application enabling the non-default UNWRAP_SINGLE_VALUE_ARRAYS feature and exposing deserialization of primitive/bean-typed data to untrusted JSON; that deployment condition cannot be confirmed from this snapshot.
jackson-core is not part of this snapshot, so its parser behavior (absence of a default nesting-depth cap in 2.13) is external knowledge rather than files inspected here.
The P1 index is syntactic only (no flow/reachability), and javadoc HTML/attic legacy trees were not audited line-by-line, so an injected or latent issue there would not be reflected in this review.

rejected_leads.lead: Independent unbounded recursion in BeanDeserializer._deserializeUsingPropertyBased (sibling CVE-2022-42004-style report)
rejected_leads.reason: Read the method (lines 411-521) and BuilderBasedDeserializer's variant (lines 359-449); no self-recursion or input-non-consuming recursion exists there beyond ordinary nested-property deserialization. The concrete unbounded recursion reachable from that entry point is the _deserializeFromArray unwrap path already included in the candidate, so it was not treated as a separate candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: Weakened polymorphic subtype validation / default-typing gadget deserialization
rejected_leads.reason: SubTypeValidator blacklist (through databind#3003 entries), LaissezFaire/DefaultBaseTypeLimiting/Basic PolymorphicTypeValidator behavior, MapperConfig.getPolymorphicTypeValidator + MapperFeature.BLOCK_UNSAFE_POLYMORPHIC_BASE_TYPES, StdTypeResolverBuilder.verifyBaseTypeValidity, DatabindContext.resolveAndValidateSubType/_resolveAndValidateGeneric, ClassNameIdResolver and MinimalClassNameIdResolver all matched expected hardened behavior; no removed validation or check was found, so this remained an unconfirmed lead rather than a finding.

rejected_leads.lead: XXE in DOMDeserializer or unsafe ObjectInput allocation in NodeSerialization
rejected_leads.reason: DOMDeserializer sets FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING, disallow-doctype-decl and load-external-dtd=false; NodeSerialization._read caps eager allocation at 100k and chunk-reads longer payloads. Both appeared hardened, so no candidate was raised.

rejected_leads.lead: Class initialization side effects via TypeFactory.findClass (Class.forName(..., initialize=true)) on attacker-supplied type ids
rejected_leads.reason: Long-standing upstream behavior reached only after polymorphic subtype validation/blacklist checks that appear intact here; no evidence of an injected regression, so not selected.

summary: Snapshot is the jackson-databind 2.13.4-SNAPSHOT main source tree (462 Java files under src/main/java; the other ~17.5k files are generated javadoc under docs/). No src/test or build execution is available. Review focused on untrusted-input paths: polymorphic type resolution/validation (SubTypeValidator, PolymorphicTypeValidator impls, MapperConfig.getPolymorphicTypeValidator, StdTypeResolverBuilder, ClassNameIdResolver/MinimalClassNameIdResolver, DatabindContext.resolveAndValidateSubType, ObjectMapper default-typing wiring), DOM/XML and node JDK-serialization helpers, ClassUtil access handling, and the core deserializer recursion paths. The polymorphic-value chain appeared intact relative to its documented hardening (blacklist entries and PTV wiring present, etc.), but the UNWRAP_SINGLE_VALUE_ARRAYS "wrapper array" unwrapping paths have no nesting/depth limit and recurse without bound, which is the strongest source-evidenced issue in this snapshot (same class as the publicly documented CVE-2022-42003/42004 doS fixes later in 2.13.4.2/2.14.0).
